stem: What is the output of the following code?

options.rationale: This adds every odd number up to 9, ignoring the break.
This adds 7 as well, but the loop breaks before 7 is added.
This stops after the first two odd numbers; 5 is still added.
Only 1, 3 and 5 are added before 7 triggers the break.

explanation: continue skips the rest of the loop body for even numbers. The odd numbers 1, 3 and 5 are added. When n is 7, the condition n > 6 is true and break ends the loop before 7 is added, so the total is 1 + 3 + 5 = 9.

stem: What is the output of the following code?

options.rationale: `pass` does nothing, so every fruit is printed, including kiwi.
That would happen with `continue`; `pass` does not skip the rest of the round.
That would happen with `break`; `pass` does not end the loop.
The print is not inside the `if`, so it runs in every round.

explanation: pass is only a placeholder: it does nothing at all. When fruit is "kiwi", the if runs pass and then the program carries on with the print as usual. So all three fruits are printed on one line, each followed by a space.

stem: What is the output of the following code?

options.rationale: `break` leaves only the inner loop, so the outer loop goes on to the other days.
In each of the 3 days, the inner loop counts hours 0 and 1, then breaks: 3 × 2 = 6.
This ignores the `break`; the inner loop never gets past hour 2.
The `break` runs before `count` is increased, so hour 2 is not counted.

explanation: For each day, the inner loop counts hour 0 and hour 1. When hour is 2, break ends the inner loop before the count line runs. break only leaves the innermost loop, so the outer loop continues with the next day. 3 days × 2 hours = 6.

stem: What happens when the following code runs?
code:
stock = 0
if stock == 0:
    print("Sold out")
    break

options.text: It prints `Sold out` and then the program ends normally.
options.rationale: An `if` is not a loop, so there is nothing for `break` to leave.

options.text: It prints `Sold out`, then stops with an error on the last line.
options.rationale: The error is found while Python reads the program, before anything runs, so nothing is printed.

options.text: Python reports a `SyntaxError` and prints nothing.
options.rationale: `break` is only allowed inside a loop, and Python checks this before it runs any line.

options.text: It prints nothing and finishes without raising any error at all.
options.rationale: `break` outside a loop is not ignored; it is an error.

explanation: break can only be used inside a for or while loop. Here it is inside an if, which is not a loop. Python checks the whole program before running it, finds SyntaxError: 'break' outside loop, and runs nothing, so Sold out is never printed.

options.text: `continue` skips the rest of the current round and goes on to the next round.
options.rationale: This is exactly what `continue` does; the loop itself keeps running.

options.text: `pass` does nothing, and the lines after it in the same block still run.
options.rationale: `pass` is only a placeholder for a place that needs a statement.
Ending the loop is what `break` does; `pass` has no effect at all.
`continue` only skips the rest of this round; the next round still runs.

options.text: In nested loops, `break` leaves all the loops at once.
options.rationale: `break` leaves only the innermost loop it is in.

options.text: A loop body may be left empty if it does nothing.
options.rationale: An empty block is an `IndentationError`; you need at least one line, such as `pass`.

explanation: continue jumps to the next round, skipping the lines below it. pass does nothing: it fills a place where Python needs at least one statement, and the lines after it still run. Only break ends a loop early, and only the innermost one.

stem: Choose the keyword that makes the program print only the positive prices, `4`, `9` and `6`, each on its own line.

blanks.rationale: `continue` skips the print for -2 and 0 but lets the loop carry on. `break` would stop at -2 after printing only 4, and `pass` would print every number.

explanation: For -2 and 0 the condition n <= 0 is true, and continue skips the rest of that round, so the print does not run. The loop then goes on with the next number, so 4, 9 and 6 are printed.

stem: Which line, inserted at the marked spot, makes the program print `1 3 5`?

This ends the whole loop at 2, so only 1 is printed.
